source.runtime_provenance: an explicit --dsh-home given on the command line; the path is deliberately not recorded (iron law 5)
source.composition: the profile as it exists on the machine that ran this: not selected by us, and not a random sample of the ecosystem

self_check.note: the control run (target == running runtime) must deny nothing new and must name the same modules as `why`; a vacuous comparison is reported as vacuous

checks.detail: every would-be-denied unit has at least one remediation
every cannot-tell unit says which evidence would resolve it
row-scope carries the row id the user must disable
0 newly denied at target==current (0 denied in total, all already denied today)
no home-shaped path in the impact payload
exit 0 (a failed lookup is not a failed run)
every unit keeps its bucket/cause with the registry path on

limits: this is a DECLARATION-layer judgement: nothing here booted 0.2.2-rc.1, so it says which rows would be denied, not whether the plugins work
the target version was not verified to exist: the run is offline by construction (no --registry), so a hypothetical target is legitimate input and an unverified one
one profile (web) on one machine: the answer does not transfer to another profile, another dsh home, or another os/arch (BS-38)
only units that are installed here were judged; a plugin that is not in this profile has no row and no answer
remediation prose and reason prose are not copied into this artifact; per-unit message ids (`reason_ids`) and fix kinds (`fix_kinds`) are, and `dsh-triage upgrade --json` carries the full lists

the `why` cross-check is VACUOUS on this profile: nothing is denied at the running runtime, so "the sets are equal" proves only that both are empty; the discriminating evidence is the same rows going 0 → N when the target moves
`unmet` lists the declared requirements that failed, capped by nothing: a plugin with 29 pinned peers contributes 29 rows here
the composition is a real profile read from an explicit --dsh-home: it is the user's own install set, so the counts describe that machine and nothing else

the target is newer relative to the running runtime: 0.1.0-rc.6 → 0.2.2-rc.1. Today no published plugin declares a range that denies 0.1.0-rc.6 and is admitted by a NEWER build (scripts/scan_upgrade_declarations.mjs scanned the registry and found none), so the real shape of "improved" is "move back to the build your plugins pin"

the `--registry` run was made unreachable on purpose (HTTP(S)_PROXY → 127.0.0.1:9), so what it proves is the failure path: the same units kept every bucket and count and the lookups were recorded as annotations; what a *successful* registry lookup would suggest is not evidenced here
